Propose a modal resolution from an AMD analysis

Source: R/amd_predictor.R
predict_amd.Rd

Optional assistance for interpreting a complete AMD curve. It computes the frozen c = 2,...,14 AMD analysis (unless a compatible curve is supplied), derives curve, data, and candidate-partition descriptors, and applies five externally loaded random forests. Reliability estimates the chance that the emitted one-versus-several-modes decision, or the exact proposed K, is correct within the assessed simulation domain. It is not directly the probability that groups exist. The target is the numerically resolved number of density modes used as the simulation reference, not necessarily the number of generating components. AMD itself does not estimate a density.

Usage

predict_amd(
  data,
  predictor,
  curve = NULL,
  seed = 1L,
  allow_extrapolation = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  max_working_bytes = 512 * 1024^2
)

Arguments

data

Numeric matrix or data frame, with observations in rows.

predictor

An object returned by load_amd_predictor().

curve

Optional compatible amd_curve. Supplying it avoids repeating the principal AMD fits; it is checked against data and the frozen model contract.

seed

Positive integer controlling AMD starts, stability refits, and any large-data sampling used by descriptors. The caller's random-number state is preserved.

allow_extrapolation

Logical. Away from the validated numerical grid, retain calibrated numerical values but label interpolation or extrapolation as unvalidated instead of suppressing them.

verbose

Logical; report progress while computing a new curve.

max_working_bytes

Positive finite working-memory guard for the exact descriptors (default 512 MiB). The estimate is not a guarantee of total process memory and excludes the externally loaded forests. The frozen global-distance summaries use a seeded sample of 2000 rows when N > 2000; partition distances remain exact. This distinction is recorded in the resource diagnostics. No additional approximation bypasses the guard.

Value

An object of class "amd_prediction" containing the AMD curve, proposed numerically resolved density-mode count K, separate structure and exact-modal-count reliability estimates, candidate scores, five-seed proposals, diagnostics, and applicability.

Details

This function does not replace inspection of the AMD curve, does not claim that its proposal is ground truth, and does not assign observations. When K > 1 is proposed, use assign_configurations() with the returned curve and a scientifically justified c.

The corrected forests use the documented missing-left-pair convention. Their unchanged historical calibrators were reassessed retrospectively on the previously examined final bank, not on a new prospective validation. Certainties are suppressed by default outside the numerical validation grid N = 150 or 600, D = 2, 6 or 15. Matching this grid does not certify the geometry of new data. The observed validation output support was K=1:8, although the mechanical candidate range is 1:14. Constant predictors dropped during training include the zero-variance fraction (always zero) and the minimum covariance-rank fraction (always one). A departure from those constants suppresses certainty, even on the numeric grid. This safeguard does not certify all other aspects of new-data geometry.

Supplying a compatible curve avoids its 260 principal fits. The additional five computational restarts per c required by the reader are still run; these are not a bootstrap or other sample-level stability analysis. Curve checks establish row/dimension and objective consistency with the supplied data, not a cryptographic identity of a separately created data file.
